name: THE LANE
materialIdentity: Cramped wooden fronts on a narrow mud lane at night: the undertaker's, the photographer's lit window, the painted tent, the barber's pole, a boarded shop (errata 161)
note: Room 44, errata 43's Room 2c: off Main Street's alley, and through to Lower Street at its far end. Built at errata 161. Lines EXTRACTED from doc 97 and compiled by tools/compile-room.mjs from reference/room-44/annotation.json.

LOOK_AT.say: A barber's pole, painted to look as though it turns. It doesn't.
repeat: There's a light under the door. A barber-surgeon in a mining camp keeps a doctor's hours.
I could do with a shave. I could do with the price of a shave more.
then: That is the first lie a barber tells you.

LISTEN_TO.say: The pole creaking in its bracket. It would turn if it could.
repeat: A strop swaying on its hook inside, slapping the chair once.
Nothing. A barber's shop is never quiet by day; at night it makes up for it.

overrides.TALK_TO: I asked for a trim. The pole said nothing, which is more than most barbers manage.

LOOK_AT.say: A pine coffin standing on end by the undertaker's door, like a man waiting to be let in.
repeat: Plain pine, nicely planed. Somebody is going to be very comfortable in that.
Standard length. A tall man would have to be very patient in it.

LISTEN_TO.say: Hollow. A good coffin rings like a cello, and this one rings like a cheap cello.
repeat: Nothing inside. I checked by knocking, and then felt I ought to apologize.
The wind across the open end, making the only sound a coffin is allowed.

overrides.PICK_UP: It's stock. Taking it would be stealing from the one merchant whose customers never complain.
overrides.OPEN: Empty, and planed smooth inside. I closed it gently. You do.

LOOK_AT.say: The photographer's window. In the middle of it, a portrait of a distinguished gentleman in a very good collar, lit like a saint.
repeat: The gentleman in the portrait has a face you would trust with your money, which in this town is a professional qualification.
Portraits by appointment. I can't afford the appointment, but I could stand here and be photographed by accident.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. The gentleman in the window has been holding very still for a long time.
repeat: A clock inside, very slow, as if it were sitting for its portrait.
Glass plates clinking in the back, being careful with each other.

overrides.TALK_TO: I asked the gentleman in the portrait for directions. He kept his counsel, and his collar.

LOOK_AT.say: An empty storefront, boarded, its sign painted out.
repeat: Through a gap in the boards: dark, and a smell of old sawdust. Whatever was sold here, it sold out.
If I strike it rich, I'll buy this and sell something. I don't yet know what. In Consolation that has never stopped anybody.
then: Somebody's whole idea, closed for good.

repeat: A loose board, lifting and settling with the wind.
Nothing. The quiet of a shop with nothing to sell and nobody to sell it.

overrides.OPEN: Boarded with long nails, by somebody who meant it.

LOOK_AT.say: Madame Ozymandia's tent, painted with more stars than the sky can spare.
repeat: The flap is tied back and candlelight comes out. It is the most inviting door in Consolation, which is why I keep a hand on my pocket.
The stars on the canvas don't quite line up with the ones above it. Neither, I suspect, do the predictions.

LISTEN_TO.say: Humming, low and long, from inside.
repeat: A brass rod, set down carefully on a table.
The canvas moving with the wind. It sounds like the tent is thinking about me.
then: Either a lady concentrating or a lady charging.

overrides.PUSH: You don't push a fortune-teller's tent. She'll have seen it coming, and she'll charge.

LOOK_AT.say: The Lane: the street the town keeps for the businesses it doesn't put on the main one.
repeat: Wide enough for two men to pass, provided they have agreed on something first.
Puddles all the way down, each one holding a lamp. It is the best-lit the Lane will ever be.

LISTEN_TO.say: Main Street at one end, Lower Street at the other, and in between a hush you could rent.
repeat: A shutter knocking, then thinking better of it.
The tent's canvas, breathing, two doors down. The Lane has a pulse and it's hers.
